english: Let $f:[-1,1]\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x+\sqrt{3-3x^{2}}}{2}\right)+\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x-\sqrt{3-3x^{2}}}{2}\right)$, where $\cos^{-1}$ takes values in $[0,\pi]$. Then the value of $\dfrac{1}{\pi}\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{18}f\left(\cos\dfrac{k\pi}{18}\right)$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $f:[-1,1]\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x+\sqrt{3-3x^{2}}}{2}\right)+\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x-\sqrt{3-3x^{2}}}{2}\right)$ द्वारा परिभाषित है, जहाँ $\cos^{-1}$ के मान $[0,\pi]$ में हैं। तब $\dfrac{1}{\pi}\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{18}f\left(\cos\dfrac{k\pi}{18}\right)$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: Substitution: every $x\in[-1,1]$ is $\cos\theta$ for a unique $\theta\in[0,\pi]$, and then $\sin\theta\ge0$, so $\sqrt{3-3x^{2}}=\sqrt3\sin\theta$. In the sum, $x=\cos\dfrac{k\pi}{18}$ corresponds to $\theta=\dfrac{k\pi}{18}\in[0,\pi]$.
First term: $\theta-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\in\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{3},\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right]$, and $\cos^{-1}(\cos\phi)=|\phi|$ for $\phi\in[-\pi,\pi]$, so it equals $\left|\theta-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right|$.

Second term: $\theta+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\in\left[\dfrac{\pi}{3},\dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right]$. If $\theta\le\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$ it is in $[0,\pi]$ and the term is $\theta+\dfrac{\pi}{3}$; if $\theta>\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$ it exceeds $\pi$ and the term is $2\pi-\left(\theta+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=\dfrac{5\pi}{3}-\theta$.

Adding the two angles: for $0\le\theta\le\dfrac{\pi}{3}$, $f=\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}-\theta\right)+\left(\theta+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$; for $\dfrac{\pi}{3}\le\theta\le\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$, $f=\left(\theta-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)+\left(\theta+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=2\theta$; for $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\le\theta\le\pi$, $f=\left(\theta-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)+\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{3}-\theta\right)=\dfrac{4\pi}{3}$. The pieces agree at $\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ and $\theta=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$.

Now $\theta=\dfrac{k\pi}{18}$. For $k=0,1,\ldots,6$ ($\theta\le\dfrac{\pi}{3}$) each value is $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$: total $\dfrac{14\pi}{3}$. For $k=7,\ldots,11$ the values are $\dfrac{2k\pi}{18}$: total $\dfrac{\pi}{9}(7+8+9+10+11)=5\pi$. For $k=12,\ldots,18$ ($\theta\ge\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$) each value is $\dfrac{4\pi}{3}$: total $\dfrac{28\pi}{3}$.
originality_note: New: the sum of two inverse cosines whose arguments become cos(theta - pi/3) and cos(theta + pi/3) after x = cos theta is constant 2pi/3 on [1/2,1], equal to 2cos^-1 x on [-1/2,1/2] and constant 4pi/3 on [-1,-1/2]; the sum over 19 sample points reads off all three pieces (way 4). Closest known: simplifying cos^-1((x+sqrt(1-x^2))/sqrt2) type expressions. Different because: two compound-angle arguments are added and the piecewise form, not one branch, is needed.

concept_use.Simplification of Inverse trigonometric: x = cos theta turns the arguments into cos(theta -/+ pi/3), giving the piecewise form of f.
concept_use.Addition and subtractions of angles invo: The two inverse cosines are added as angles: |theta - pi/3| + (theta + pi/3) or (5pi/3 - theta), producing the constant pieces 2pi/3 and 4pi/3.
